title: Structured Log Event
description: One line of `.artifacts/telemetry/events.jsonl`. The console line is a rendering of this record, never a second source of truth, and the record is what an evidence entry cites through `eventIds`. Written by `scripts/lib/log.ts`; the same invariants are enforced there so an unsound event throws at the call site instead of being discovered later by a reader. Colour codes never appear here — an escape sequence in a captured artifact is corruption a reader has to strip before the file parses cleanly.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601, UTC. The console shows only its clock portion.

level.description: DEBUG is written to the artifact and hidden from the console at the default INFO threshold. The artifact is the evidence sink: evidence filtered at write time cannot be recovered.

eventId.description: Stable across runs and across agents — the same failure reported twice carries the same id. That is what makes deduplication and `this retry is that failure` mechanical rather than two messages a reader decides look alike.

message.description: One line, a state fact. Not a narration of what the agent is about to do.

status.description: `unknown` is a first-class value. A summary derives its verdict from these, and any unknown keeps it out of DONE.

evidenceId.description: Correlates this event with the evidence entry in a handoff. Required on PASS.

artifact.description: Repository-relative path holding the full output this line summarises.

tests.description: Present on any event reporting a suite. The summary sums these, so a count here that nobody reported cannot appear there.

failure.description: Required on ERROR and FATAL. A failure line without expected and actual costs the same to write as one somebody can act on.

classification.description: The Diagnostician's four, when a classification has actually been established. A failure log proves the failure; it does not establish its cause, so this field stays absent until something else settled it.

duplicateOf.description: The event this one repeats or propagates. A retry cites the failure it retries, and a caller re-reporting a callee's error cites the original — so one stack is written once and referenced everywhere else.
